ko: 로리가 은행 문을 열었을 때 생각한 것은, 텔슨 은행의 지붕 아래에 프랑스 망명 죄수의 아내를 머물게 함으로써 은행을 위험에 빠뜨릴 권리가 그에게 없다는 것이었다.

raw: His own possessions, safety, life, he would have hazarded for Lucie and her child, without a moment’s demur; but the great trust he held was not his own, and as to that business charge he was a strict man of business.
en: He would have risked his own money, safety, and life for Lucie and her child without hesitation. However, the bank was a trust that did not belong to him, and he had to be a strict businessman about it.
ko: 그는 루시와 그녀의 아이를 위해 주저 없이 자신의 돈과 안전, 생명을 걸었을 것이다. 그러나 은행은 그의 것이 아닌 신탁이었고, 그는 그에 대해 엄격한 사업가가 되어야 했다.

raw: At first, his mind reverted to Defarge, and he thought of finding out the wine-shop again and taking counsel with its master in reference to the safest dwelling-place in the distracted state of the city.
en: At first, he thought of Defarge, wondering if he should go back to the wine shop to ask him where the safest place to stay would be in this chaotic city.
ko: 처음에 그는 드파르지를 떠올리며, 이 혼란스러운 도시에서 가장 안전하게 머물 곳이 어디일지 그에게 묻기 위해 와인 상점으로 돌아가야 할지 고민했다.

raw: But, the same consideration that suggested him, repudiated him; he lived in the most violent Quarter, and doubtless was influential there, and deep in its dangerous workings.
en: But the same reason that made him think of Defarge also made him change his mind: Defarge lived in the most violent district, was very influential there, and was deeply involved in the dangerous revolution.
ko: 하지만 그가 드파르지를 생각하게 만든 바로 그 이유가 그의 마음을 바꾸게 했다. 드파르지는 가장 폭력적인 지역에 살고 있었고, 그곳에서 매우 큰 영향력을 행사했으며, 위험한 혁명에 깊이 관여하고 있었다.

ko: 로리는 루시와 이야기했다.

ko: 그녀는 아버지가 이 지역, 은행 근처에 잠시 동안 아파트를 빌리는 것에 대해 언급했다고 말했다.

raw: As there was no business objection to this, and as he foresaw that even if it were all well with Charles, and he were to be released, he could not hope to leave the city, Mr.
en: Since there was no business objection to this, and since Mr. Lorry realized that even if Charles were released, they could not leave the city yet, he went out to look for lodgings.
ko: 이에 대한 업무상의 반대는 없었고, 로리 역시 찰스가 풀려난다 하더라도 그들이 아직 이 도시를 떠날 수 없다는 것을 깨달았기에, 그는 숙소를 구하러 나갔다.

raw: Lorry went out in quest of such a lodging, and found a suitable one, high up in a removed by-street where the closed blinds in all the other windows of a high melancholy square of buildings marked deserted homes.
en: He found a suitable place high up in a quiet side street where the closed shutters of the other windows in a tall, gloomy square showed that the houses were empty.
ko: 그는 조용한 골목의 높은 곳에 있는 적당한 장소를 찾았는데, 그곳은 우울하고 높은 광장에 있는 다른 창문들의 닫힌 덧문들이 그 집들이 비어 있음을 보여주었다.

raw: To this lodging he at once removed Lucie and her child, and Miss Pross: giving them what comfort he could, and much more than he had himself.
en: He immediately moved Lucie, her child, and Miss Pross to this apartment, making them as comfortable as possible, much more comfortable than he was himself.
ko: 그는 즉시 루시, 그녀의 아이, 그리고 프로스 양을 이 아파트로 옮기고 그들을 가능한 한 편안하게 해 주었다. 그 자신보다 훨씬 더 편안하게 말이다.

raw: He left Jerry with them, as a figure to fill a doorway that would bear considerable knocking on the head, and returned to his own occupations.
en: He left Jerry Cruncher with them as a guard who could handle a fight if necessary, and returned to his work.
ko: 그는 필요하다면 싸움도 감당할 수 있는 경호원으로 제리 크런처를 그들과 함께 남겨두고 일터로 돌아갔다.

raw: A disturbed and doleful mind he brought to bear upon them, and slowly and heavily the day lagged on with him.
en: He felt anxious and sad, and the day dragged on slowly and heavily.
ko: 그는 불안하고 슬펐고, 하루는 느리고 무겁게 흘러갔다.

raw: It wore itself out, and wore him out with it, until the Bank closed.
en: The day finally ended, leaving him exhausted by the time the bank closed.
ko: 마침내 하루가 끝났고, 은행 문을 닫을 때쯤 그는 지쳐버렸다.

en: He was alone again in his room from the night before, thinking about what to do next, when he heard footsteps on the stairs.
ko: 그가 전날 밤에 머물렀던 방에 다시 혼자 남아 다음에 무엇을 해야 할지 생각하고 있을 때, 계단에서 발소리가 들렸다.

ko: 잠시 후, 한 남자가 들어와 그를 유심히 바라보더니 그의 이름을 불렀다.

ko: 그녀는 남편의 소식에 기쁨으로 가득 차서 드파르지가 그녀에게 쪽지를 건넬 때 그의 손에 입을 맞추었다, 그 손이 전날 밤 다네이 근처에서 무슨 짓을 하고 있었는지, 상황이 달랐다면 그 손이 그에게 무슨 짓을 했을지 상상조차 하지 못한 채.

ko: 나는 무사하고, 당신의 아버지는 이곳에서 영향력이 있소.

ko: 이 편지에 답장을 할 수는 없소.

ko: 그것이 메시지의 전부였다.

en: But it meant so much to Lucie that she turned to Madame Defarge and kissed one of the hands that was knitting.
ko: 하지만 그것은 루시에게 너무나 큰 의미였기에 그녀는 드파르지 부인에게 몸을 돌려 뜨개질을 하고 있던 그녀의 손 중 하나에 입을 맞추었다.

raw: It was a passionate, loving, thankful, womanly action, but the hand made no response--dropped cold and heavy, and took to its knitting again.
en: It was a loving, thankful gesture, but the hand did not respond, it dropped cold and heavy, and then immediately went back to its knitting.
ko: 그것은 사랑스럽고 감사한 몸짓이었지만, 그 손은 반응하지 않았고 차갑고 무겁게 떨어졌으며 즉시 다시 뜨개질로 돌아갔다.

raw: There was something in its touch that gave Lucie a check.
en: The cold feel of the hand startled Lucie.
ko: 그 차가운 손의 감촉은 루시를 깜짝 놀라게 했다.

raw: She stopped in the act of putting the note in her bosom, and, with her hands yet at her neck, looked terrified at Madame Defarge.
en: She paused as she was putting the note inside her dress, her hands frozen at her collar, and looked at Madame Defarge in fear.
ko: 그녀는 쪽지를 드레스 안에 넣다가 잠시 멈췄고 두 손이 목깃에 얼어붙은 채 두려움 속에서 드파르지 부인을 바라보았다.

raw: Madame Defarge met the lifted eyebrows and forehead with a cold, impassive stare.
en: Madame Defarge returned her worried look with a cold, blank stare.
ko: 드파르지 부인은 그녀의 걱정스러운 시선을 차갑고 무표정한 눈빛으로 돌려주었다.

raw: “My dear,” said Mr.
en: “My dear,” Mr.

raw: Lorry, striking in to explain; “there are frequent risings in the streets; and, although it is not likely they will ever trouble you, Madame Defarge wishes to see those whom she has the power to protect at such times, to the end that she may know them--that she may identify them.
en: Lorry interrupted to explain, “there are frequent riots in the streets. Although they probably won't bother you, Madame Defarge wants to see the people she has the power to protect during these times, so that she can recognize them.
ko: 설명하기 위해 끼어들었다, “거리에서 잦은 폭동이 일어나고 있습니다. 비록 그들이 당신을 괴롭히지는 않을 테지만, 드파르지 부인은 이 시기에 자신이 보호할 수 있는 사람들을 확인하고 싶어 합니다, 그래서 그녀가 그들을 알아볼 수 있도록 말입니다.

raw: I believe,” said Mr.
en: I believe,” Mr.
ko: 내 생각에,” 로리 씨는

en: Lorry said, hesitating as the cold behavior of the three visitors began to make him nervous, “I am explaining this correctly, Citizen Defarge?”
ko: 세 방문객의 차가운 행동이 그를 긴장하게 만들면서 주저하며 말했다, “제가 이것을 제대로 설명하고 있는 거 맞습니까, 시민 드파르지?”

raw: Defarge looked gloomily at his wife, and gave no other answer than a gruff sound of acquiescence.
en: Defarge looked gloomily at his wife and answered only with a rough grunt of agreement.
ko: 드파르지는 우울하게 그의 아내를 바라보며 단지 거친 콧소리로 동의의 대답만 할 뿐이었다.

raw: “You had better, Lucie,” said Mr.
en: “You had better bring the dear child here, Lucie,” Mr.

en: Lorry said, trying to sound as friendly as possible, “and our good Miss Pross.
ko: 말했다, 최대한 다정한 목소리를 내려고 노력하며, “그리고 우리의 좋은 프로스 양도요.

en: Our friend Pross, Defarge, is an English lady and doesn't speak French.”
ko: 우리의 친구 프로스는, 드파르지, 영국 숙녀이고 프랑스어를 하지 못합니다.”

raw: The lady in question, whose rooted conviction that she was more than a match for any foreigner, was not to be shaken by distress and, danger, appeared with folded arms, and observed in English to The Vengeance, whom her eyes first encountered, “Well, I am sure, Boldface!
en: Miss Pross, who firmly believed she was more than a match for any foreigner even in times of danger, came in with her arms crossed. Looking at The Vengeance, she said in English, “Well, I must say, Boldface!
ko: 위험한 때라도 어떤 외국인도 상대할 수 있다고 굳게 믿었던 프로스 양이 팔짱을 끼고 들어왔다. 복수라는 여인을 바라보며 그녀는 영어로 말했다, “글쎄요, 내가 한마디 해야겠군요, 철면피 양반!

raw: I hope _you_ are pretty well!” She also bestowed a British cough on Madame Defarge; but, neither of the two took much heed of her.
en: I hope _you_ are doing well!” She also coughed loudly at Madame Defarge, but neither woman paid any attention to her.
ko: 나는 당신이 잘 지내기를 바랍니다!” 그녀는 또한 드파르지 부인을 향해 크게 기침을 했지만, 두 여성 중 누구도 그녀에게 신경 쓰지 않았다.

raw: “Is that his child?” said Madame Defarge, stopping in her work for the first time, and pointing her knitting-needle at little Lucie as if it were the finger of Fate.
en: “Is that his child?” Madame Defarge asked, stopping her knitting for the first time and pointing her needle at little Lucie like the finger of fate.
ko: “저 아이가 그의 아이입니까?” 드파르지 부인이 물었다, 처음으로 뜨개질을 멈추고 운명의 손가락처럼 어린 루시를 향해 바늘을 가리키며.

raw: “Yes, madame,” answered Mr.
en: “Yes, madame,” Mr.
ko: “네, 부인,” 로리 씨가

raw: Lorry; “this is our poor prisoner’s darling daughter, and only child.”
en: Lorry answered. “This is our poor prisoner's darling daughter and only child.”
ko: 대답했다. “이 아이는 우리의 불쌍한 죄수의 사랑하는 딸이자 외동딸입니다.”

raw: The shadow attendant on Madame Defarge and her party seemed to fall so threatening and dark on the child, that her mother instinctively kneeled on the ground beside her, and held her to her breast.
en: The threatening presence of Madame Defarge and her companions seemed to cast such a dark shadow over the child that Lucie instinctively knelt down and held her daughter to her chest.
ko: 드파르지 부인과 그녀의 동료들의 위협적인 존재감이 아이에게 너무나 짙은 그림자를 드리우는 것 같아서 루시는 본능적으로 무릎을 꿇고 딸을 그녀의 가슴에 품었다.

raw: The shadow attendant on Madame Defarge and her party seemed then to fall, threatening and dark, on both the mother and the child.
en: The dark and threatening shadow that followed Madame Defarge and her group seemed to fall right onto both the mother and the child.
ko: 드파르지 부인과 그녀의 일행을 따라온 어둡고 위협적인 그림자가 어머니와 아이 모두에게 바로 떨어지는 듯했다.

raw: “It is enough, my husband,” said Madame Defarge. “I have seen them.
en: “It is enough, husband,” Madame Defarge said. “I have seen them.
ko: “충분해요, 여보,” 드파르지 부인이 말했다. “내가 그들을 보았소.

raw: We may go.”
en: We can go.”
ko: 이제 가도 됩니다.”

raw: But, the suppressed manner had enough of menace in it--not visible and presented, but indistinct and withheld--to alarm Lucie into saying, as she laid her appealing hand on Madame Defarge’s dress:
en: But her quiet behavior carried such a hidden threat that Lucie was frightened into saying, grabbing Madame Defarge's dress pleadingly:
ko: 그러나 그녀의 조용한 행동에는 그런 숨겨진 위협이 담겨 있어서 루시는 겁에 질려 드파르지 부인의 드레스를 애원하듯 붙잡으며 말했다:

raw: “You will be good to my poor husband.
en: “Please be kind to my poor husband.
ko: “제 불쌍한 남편에게 자비를 베풀어주세요.

raw: You will do him no harm.
en: Do not let them hurt him.
ko: 그들이 그를 해치지 않게 해주세요.

raw: You will help me to see him if you can?”
en: Will you help me see him if you can?”
ko: 할 수 있으시다면 제가 그를 볼 수 있도록 도와주시겠어요?”

raw: “Your husband is not my business here,” returned Madame Defarge, looking down at her with perfect composure. “It is the daughter of your father who is my business here.”
en: “Your husband is not my concern here,” Madame Defarge replied, looking down at her calmly. “I came here to see the daughter of your father.”
ko: “당신의 남편은 여기서 내 알 바가 아닙니다,” 드파르지 부인이 침착하게 그녀를 내려다보며 대답했다. “나는 당신 아버지의 딸을 보러 이곳에 왔습니다.”

raw: “For my sake, then, be merciful to my husband.
en: “For my sake, then, show mercy to my husband!
ko: “그렇다면 저를 봐서라도, 제 남편에게 자비를 베풀어주세요!

raw: For my child’s sake!
en: For my child's sake!
ko: 제 아이를 위해서라도요!

raw: She will put her hands together and pray you to be merciful.
en: She will fold her hands and beg you to be merciful.
ko: 그 아이가 두 손을 모으고 당신에게 자비를 베풀어 달라고 애원할 것입니다.

raw: We are more afraid of you than of these others.”
en: We are more afraid of you than of anyone else.”
ko: 우리는 그 누구보다 당신이 더 두렵습니다.”

raw: Madame Defarge received it as a compliment, and looked at her husband.
en: Madame Defarge took this as a compliment and looked at her husband.
ko: 드파르지 부인은 이것을 칭찬으로 받아들이고 그녀의 남편을 쳐다보았다.

raw: Defarge, who had been uneasily biting his thumb-nail and looking at her, collected his face into a sterner expression.
en: Defarge, who had been nervously biting his nail and watching her, forced his face into a stern expression.
ko: 드파르지는 신경질적으로 손톱을 물어뜯으며 그녀를 지켜보고 있었는데 억지로 엄격한 표정을 지었다.

raw: “What is it that your husband says in that little letter?” asked Madame Defarge, with a lowering smile. “Influence; he says something touching influence?”
en: “What does your husband say in that little letter?” Madame Defarge asked with a dark smile. “Influence? Did he mention something about influence?”
ko: “당신의 남편이 그 작은 편지에서 뭐라고 하던가요?” 드파르지 부인이 어두운 미소를 지으며 물었다. “영향력? 그가 영향력에 대해 무언가 말했습니까?”

raw: “That my father,” said Lucie, hurriedly taking the paper from her breast, but with her alarmed eyes on her questioner and not on it, “has much influence around him.”
en: “He says my father,” Lucie said, quickly pulling out the paper but keeping her eyes fixed on Madame Defarge, “has a lot of influence there.”
ko: “그는 제 아버지가,” 루시가 말했다, 재빨리 종이를 꺼내면서도 시선은 드파르지 부인에게 고정시킨 채로, “그곳에서 많은 영향력을 가지고 있다고 말했습니다.”

raw: “Surely it will release him!” said Madame Defarge. “Let it do so.”
en: “Then surely it will set him free!” Madame Defarge said. “Let it do that.”
ko: “그렇다면 분명히 그것이 그를 자유롭게 할 것입니다!” 드파르지 부인이 말했다. “그렇게 되도록 두십시오.”

raw: “As a wife and mother,” cried Lucie, most earnestly, “I implore you to have pity on me and not to exercise any power that you possess, against my innocent husband, but to use it in his behalf.
en: “As a wife and mother,” Lucie cried out very seriously, “I beg you to have pity on me! Please don't use any power you have against my innocent husband, but instead use it to help him.”
ko: “한 명의 아내이자 어머니로서,” 루시가 아주 진지하게 외쳤다, “당신이 저를 가엾게 여겨주시길 간청합니다! 제발 당신이 가진 어떤 권력도 제 무고한 남편에게 불리하게 사용하지 마시고, 대신 그를 돕기 위해 사용해 주세요.”

raw: O sister-woman, think of me.
en: Do not use your power against my innocent husband, but help him instead.
ko: 제 무고한 남편을 대항하여 당신의 힘을 사용하지 말고, 대신 그를 도와주세요.

raw: As a wife and mother!”
en: Oh, think of me as another woman, as a wife and mother!”
ko: 오, 저를 다른 여인처럼, 한 아내이자 어머니로서 생각해 주세요!”

raw: Madame Defarge looked, coldly as ever, at the suppliant, and said, turning to her friend The Vengeance:
en: Madame Defarge looked at the pleading woman as coldly as ever, and turned to her friend The Vengeance:
ko: 드파르지 부인은 애원하는 여인을 평소와 다름없이 차갑게 바라보고 그녀의 친구인 복수라는 여인에게 고개를 돌렸다:

raw: “The wives and mothers we have been used to see, since we were as little as this child, and much less, have not been greatly considered?
en: “Have the wives and mothers we have seen since we were children ever been treated with mercy?
ko: “우리가 어릴 때부터 보아온 아내와 어머니들이 자비로운 대우를 받은 적이 있소?

raw: We have known _their_ husbands and fathers laid in prison and kept from them, often enough?
en: Haven't we seen _their_ husbands and fathers thrown in prison and kept from them for years?
ko: 우리는 그들의 남편과 아버지들이 감옥에 던져지고 수년 동안 그들로부터 떨어져 지내는 것을 보지 않았소?

raw: All our lives, we have seen our sister-women suffer, in themselves and in their children, poverty, nakedness, hunger, thirst, sickness, misery, oppression and neglect of all kinds?”
en: All our lives, haven't we watched other women and their children suffer poverty, starvation, sickness, pain, and oppression?”
ko: 우리 평생 동안 다른 여성들과 그들의 아이들이 가난, 기아, 질병, 고통, 그리고 억압에 시달리는 것을 지켜보지 않았소?”

raw: “We have seen nothing else,” returned The Vengeance.
en: “We have seen nothing else,” The Vengeance replied.
ko: “우리는 다른 것은 보지 못했습니다,” 복수라는 여인이 대답했다.

raw: “We have borne this a long time,” said Madame Defarge, turning her eyes again upon Lucie. “Judge you! Is it likely that the trouble of one wife and mother would be much to us now?”
en: “We have suffered this for a very long time,” Madame Defarge said, turning back to Lucie. “So tell me: why should the trouble of one single wife and mother matter to us now?”
ko: “우리는 이 일로 아주 오랫동안 고통받아 왔소,” 드파르지 부인이 루시에게 다시 고개를 돌리며 말했다. “그러니 말해보시오: 단 한 명의 아내이자 어머니의 곤경이 지금 우리에게 왜 중요해야 합니까?”

raw: She resumed her knitting and went out.
en: She went back to her knitting and walked out of the room.
ko: 그녀는 다시 뜨개질로 돌아가서 방을 걸어 나갔다.

raw: The Vengeance followed. Defarge went last, and closed the door.
en: The Vengeance followed her, and Defarge left last, closing the door behind him.
ko: 복수라는 여인이 그녀를 따랐고, 드파르지가 뒤로 문을 닫으며 마지막으로 떠났다.

raw: “Courage, my dear Lucie,” said Mr.
en: “Have courage, my dear Lucie,” Mr.
ko: “용기를 가지시오, 내 사랑하는 루시,” 로리 씨가

raw: Lorry, as he raised her. “Courage, courage!
en: Lorry said as he helped her up. “Courage, courage!
ko: 그녀가 일어나는 것을 도우며 말했다. “용기, 용기를 내요!

raw: So far all goes well with us--much, much better than it has of late gone with many poor souls.
en: So far, everything is going well for us, much better than for many other poor souls.
ko: 지금까지는, 다른 많은 불쌍한 사람들보다 훨씬 더 우리를 위해 모든 일이 잘 진행되고 있습니다.

raw: Cheer up, and have a thankful heart.”
en: Cheer up and try to be hopeful.”
ko: 기운을 내고 희망을 가져보시오.”

raw: “I am not thankless, I hope, but that dreadful woman seems to throw a shadow on me and on all my hopes.”
en: “I am not ungrateful, but that terrifying woman seems to cast a dark shadow over all my hopes.”
ko: “제가 감사할 줄 모르는 것이 아니지만, 그 무서운 여자가 제 모든 희망에 어두운 그림자를 드리우는 것 같아요.”

raw: “Tut, tut!” said Mr.
en: “Come, come!” Mr.
ko: “자, 자!” 로리 씨가

raw: Lorry; “what is this despondency in the brave little breast?
en: Lorry said. “Why is my brave girl losing heart?
ko: 말했다. “왜 나의 용감한 소녀가 낙심하는 걸까요?

raw: A shadow indeed!
en: A shadow is just a shadow!
ko: 그림자는 그저 그림자일 뿐이오!

raw: No substance in it, Lucie.”
en: There is nothing real to fear in it, Lucie.”
ko: 그 안에 진짜 두려워할 것은 아무것도 없소, 루시.”

raw: But the shadow of the manner of these Defarges was dark upon himself, for all that, and in his secret mind it troubled him greatly.
en: But the dark attitude of the Defarges worried Mr. Lorry deeply as well, though he kept his fears to himself.
ko: 하지만 드파르지 부부의 어두운 태도는 로리 씨에게도 깊은 걱정을 안겨주었고, 비록 그는 자신의 두려움을 마음속에 간직했지만 말이다.
